definitions.gloss: side mirror; wing mirror; door-mounted mirror
definitions.explanation: The exterior mirror mounted on a car door for checking the rear and side views while driving. A wasei-eigo term (door + mirror) that is standard in Japanese automotive vocabulary.

examples.japanese: ドアミラーを{調整|ちょうせい}してください。
{車線変更|しゃせんへんこう}の{前|まえ}にドアミラーを{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: Check the side mirror before changing lanes.

examples.japanese: {狭|せま}い{道|みち}でドアミラーを{擦|こす}ってしまい、{修理|しゅうり}に{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I scraped the side mirror on a narrow road and had to get it repaired.

notes:
A wasei-eigo compound (English "door" + "mirror"). In English, the same part is called a "side mirror," "wing mirror" (British), or "side-view mirror." The Japanese term emphasizes the mounting location (on the door) rather than the function.

Older Japanese cars used フェンダーミラー (fender mirrors) mounted on the front fenders. Japan was one of the last countries to allow ドアミラー, which became legal in 1983 and quickly became standard. Fender mirrors are now rare but still seen on some taxis.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドアミラーを{調整|ちょうせい}する: to adjust the side mirror
- ドアミラーを{確認|かくにん}する: to check the side mirror
- ドアミラーを{畳|たた}む: to fold in the side mirror
- {電動|でんどう}ドアミラー: power-folding side mirror

RELATED WORDS:
- フェンダーミラー: fender mirror — older style, mounted on front fender
- バックミラー: rearview mirror — the interior mirror
- ルームミラー: room mirror — another term for the interior rearview mirror
- サイドミラー: side mirror — less common synonym of ドアミラー
